text:
Neither starter shows up for this one. San Jose gives Alex Nedeljkovic the night over Yaroslav Askarov, and that's less of a downgrade than it sounds: Nedeljkovic has a .901 save rate in nine games and is 7.2 goals better than expected, the best number of anyone in either crease tonight. Anaheim goes to Laurent Brossoit, five games in, at .866. In front of them are two defenses that give away a lot. The Sharks allow the second-most expected goals per 60 (the quality of chances against), and our numbers have the Ducks at 3.90 expected goals and San Jose at 3.14.

Anaheim's story is Cutter Gauthier and the hole around him. Gauthier is in the Rocket Richard race with Leon Draisaitl, had a goal streak long enough to make the history pages before Colorado ended it, and has 16 points in ten games. We have him at 47% to score. But the Ducks are winless in four, and now Leo Carlsson (29 points in 24 games) is out with an upper-body injury on top of Beckett Sennecke (26 in 22) on injured reserve. That's two of their top scorers gone at once. Troy Terry's ice time has jumped past 20 minutes, and Tim Washe has moved into Carlsson's spot. Our depth sleeper is fourth-liner Nikita Nesterenko, at 13% to score after a run of dangerous shots.

San Jose has its own young centre. Macklin Celebrini has ten points in four career games against Anaheim, and we have him at 47% for two or more points. Ivar Stenberg, the rookie on his wing, is our point sleeper at 53%, above his season pace, because his line creates 3.80 expected goals per 60. Dmitry Orlov has 11 points in ten and is one assist from 300. Collin Graf returns, and Kiefer Sherwood and Igor Chernyshov stay out.

The Sharks take 45% of the five-on-five expected goals, the Ducks 46%. It's the first meeting of the season, and the Ducks sit at 36% to make the playoffs, the Sharks at 6%.
headline: Backups in net for a California mess
